question: What engineering change, intervention, or design would prevent or mitigate the stated failure under the stated constraint, and what concrete test would falsify the proposed approach?
device: laminated elastomeric bridge bearing pad on a 75-year-design-life highway bridge
failure: elastomer layers develop creep set and ozone surface crazing over decades; vertical deflection drift exceeds design tolerance
followup_finding: The last 4 bearing pad replacements on this bridge class showed the inside layers failing first — ozone exposure is limited to the exterior layers where crazing starts. The failed pads had no exterior surface protection.
constraint: intervention must extend bearing life to 75 years without replacing the bearing; no new instrumentation required; must tolerate marine climate
round1_answer:
Optimization of hydrogenated natural rubber (HNR) compound using semi-efficient vulcanization system and N220 carbon black filler to improve rubber-filler interaction and crosslink network rigidity, addressing low interaction and inadequate compression set properties.

Replace standard natural rubber core layers with HNR compounded with N220 carbon black and a semi-efficient vulcanization system; apply a marine-grade exterior protection layer to the outermost elastomer surfaces to shield against ozone.

Extended bearing life to 75 years with reduced creep set, improved compression set performance, and elimination of exterior ozone crazing, while maintaining vertical deflection within tolerance.

Subject accelerated weathering and compression set tests to HNR/N220 prototype pads with and without exterior protection; verify that unprotected pads fail before 75-year equivalent stress while protected pads meet AASHTO M251 compression set and ozone resistance standards.
round2_answer:
Modifying the vulcanization system to "semi efficient" and utilizing specific carbon black filler (N220) to enhance rubber-filler interaction and crosslink network rigidity, thereby reducing compression set in hydrogenated natural rubber (HNR).

Retrofit the interior elastomer layers of the existing laminated bearing pads by overlaying or replacing them with a pre-vulcanized HNR compound specifically formulated with N220 carbon black and a semi-efficient vulcanization system. This material swap targets the "inside layers failing first" issue identified in the field return, replacing the standard natural/chloroprene rubber with HNR to lower creep set. The exterior layers should be sealed with a protective polymeric coating to block ozone, while the new HNR interior provides improved dimensional stability.

Vertical deflection drift is reduced below design tolerance by minimizing compression set in the high-stress interior layers, extending the service life to 75 years without full bearing replacement.

Subject a mock-up bearing pad containing the new HNR/N220/semi-efficient interior layers to ASTM D1414 Type III compression set testing at 70°C for 22 hours; if the compression set exceeds 25%, the mechanism fails to prevent long-term vertical drift.
